description: crl.rs check_revocation_against_anchor, lines 400-410: the delta CRL path calls verify_delta_crl_and_collect with the anchor's subject/SPKI. This is correct if the base CRL and the delta CRL have the same issuer, but the anchor path does NOT perform the defense-in-depth cross-check that check_revocation does at lines 282-291 (verify delta issuer == base CRL issuer AND cert issuer before calling the helper). If the delta CRL's issuer DN were somehow different from the base CRL's issuer DN (e.g., a corrupt or substituted delta), the anchor path would only catch it via the verify_delta_crl_and_collect name match (anchor.subject), while the cert's issuer check is also absent. The non-anchor path has three name checks; the anchor path has one. Practically the missing check is mitigated by with_delta() validating issuer names at construction, but that validation is bypassed if someone constructs CrlChecker with a raw field access. The defense-in-depth pattern is inconsistent between the two paths. Suggested fix: add the same guard before calling verify_delta_crl_and_collect in check_revocation_against_anchor: verify that the parsed delta issuer matches both the base CRL issuer and cert.tbs_certificate.issuer (via anchor.subject).
title: P0: Delta CRL anchor path missing cross-check vs base CRL issuer
